scenario: A 33-year-old female is brought to the ED unresponsive after being dragged out of a house fire, with significant burns, soot on the face, singed eyebrows, hypotension, tachycardia, and profound altered mental status. The scenario focuses on intubation, fluid resuscitation, recognition of CO/CN poisoning, hydroxycobalamin treatment, and arrest if cyanide toxicity is not treated.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: She's GCS 3 and can't protect her airway, so we're intubating now with RSI. Draw up the RSI meds and get suction ready, and bag her up first.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: RSI meds are in, pre-oxygenated with BVM. Ready for your intubation attempt.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Get me a post-intubation chest X-ray to confirm tube position.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: She's hypotensive at 70/42 with a heart rate of 124. Start a liter of normal saline wide open.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Starting the 1 liter normal saline bolus now.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Send a carboxyhemoglobin level on her. I want to rule out a CO or toxic cause for her being unresponsive.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Post-intubation CXR is back: normal, tube position confirmed. Carboxyhemoglobin is sent, results pending. Still hypotensive at 74/44, HR 125, sats 97% on the vent.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: She's still hypotensive at 74/44 after the full liter. Start norepinephrine and titrate up.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Norepinephrine started and running.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Carboxyhemoglobin is back at 0.4 — negative, no CO. On the norepi she's up to 85/49, HR 128, sats 97% on the vent.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Send a venous blood gas with lactate — I need her acid-base status to guide where we go with the norepi.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: VBG is back: pH 6.98, PCO2 28, PO2 70, HCO3 6, lactate 11. Severe high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis with partial respiratory compensation. She's on 85/49, HR 128, sats 97% on the vent.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: That pH of 6.98 with a bicarb of 6 and lactate of 11 is life-threatening acidosis. Push an amp of IV sodium bicarbonate now, and keep the norepinephrine running.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Get me a 12-lead ECG now. I'm looking for any ischemia, arrhythmia, or QRS or QT changes that could point to a toxic or metabolic cause for this acidosis.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: 12-lead is back: sinus tachycardia, no ischemic changes, no QRS widening or QT prolongation. After the bicarb she's 70/42, HR 138, sats 97% on the vent.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: She's still crashing — 70/42 with a lactate of 11. Give another liter of normal saline wide open and keep the norepinephrine running.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: She's still in refractory shock at 70/42, HR 138, despite fluids and norepi. Start epinephrine as a second pressor alongside the norepinephrine.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Her pH is still critically low at 6.98 — push another amp of IV sodium bicarbonate now, and keep both the norepinephrine and epinephrine running.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Start fomepizole now empirically — this severe unexplained anion-gap acidosis fits a toxic alcohol ingestion. Keep both the norepinephrine and epinephrine running.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Fomepizole is in and running.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Start folinic acid now as an adjunct for suspected toxic alcohol ingestion, and keep both the norepinephrine and epinephrine running. And get dialysis on the phone — she needs urgent hemodialysis for this acidosis.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Folinic acid is in and running.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Draw a repeat venous blood gas now — I need to see where her pH, bicarb, and lactate are after the bicarb, antidotes, and pressors before we commit to dialysis.
